title: Republic of the Rio Grande
capsule: The Republic of the Rio Grande was a short-lived separatist state proclaimed on 17 January 1840 in the town of Laredo by federalist rebels in the Mexican states of Tamaulipas, Nuevo León, and Coahuila, opposing Santa Anna's centralist constitution of 1836. Led by Antonio Canales Rosillo, the republic attracted some Texan volunteer support and initially scored military successes, but the movement fractured when promised Texan annexation did not materialise and Mexican federal forces under General Mariano Arista pressed the rebels hard. Canales surrendered and accepted amnesty on 6 November 1840, extinguishing the republic after less than ten months of existence. The episode reflected the broader instability of northern Mexican frontier society and the gravitational pull of the Republic of Texas on disaffected borderland populations.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The claimed territory of the Republic of the Rio Grande is described in its proclamation documents but was never effectively controlled in full; actual military presence was confined to scattered towns along the Rio Grande, making any territorial map highly speculative.
